name: Syria

findings.local_actor: Syriatel and MTN Syria (the two mobile operators)
findings.summary: Reuters, relayed by Al-Monitor and Enab Baladi, reported that Huawei supplies over half of the infrastructure of both Syrian mobile operators, Syriatel and MTN, citing an operator source and documents.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei as equipment vendor, so pole prc. Tier 5 for an installed, operating base; the >50% share is Reuters' figure, not split into RAN/core. Both opened reports relay a single Reuters story, so not independent, and neither is S1/S2. still_current null: reported as current in Feb 2026, not reconfirmed since. Original install dates unknown (likely pre-2011).

findings.controller: Not established (equipment vendor not named); stc Group (Saudi Arabia) is the contracted deployer
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (SilkLink project)
findings.summary: Saudi operator stc said it won a competitive tender and signed a contract for Syria's SilkLink project: a 4,500 km national fibre network, data centres and international subsea cable landing stations, valued at SAR 3bn (about USD 800m).
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: under the equipment-vendor rule the controller is whoever supplies the fibre/transmission gear, which no source names. If stc operates the network it would be third (Gulf); not documented. USD 800m is the project valuation in SAR 3bn; stc did not disclose its contract value, and an unopened headline gives 675m (currency unclear). Both opened reports likely derive from stc's own disclosure; reviewer may discount corroboration. Data-centre and cable-landing components not coded separately (no detail).

findings.controller: Not specified (owner-operator of planned national data centre unstated)
findings.summary: Saudi telco GO (Etihad Atheeb) signed a non-binding MoU with Syria's communications ministry to help provide a national data centre and support e-government, AI, IoT and cloud services; value and site undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: MoU explicitly not legally enforceable. Pole null because owner-operator is unstated; GO would make it third if it owns or operates the facility. No follow-up contract found.

findings.controller: aiXplain (US-headquartered, San Jose; MENA HQ Riyadh)
findings.summary: Syriatel and aiXplain signed an MoU, ratified at LEAP in Riyadh, to deploy Arabic-first AI infrastructure across Syriatel's network; engineers already use an aiXplain coding tool while a customer-service agent is in development.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on aiXplain's headquarters as the service provider; aiXplain is an agent/orchestration platform and the underlying model(s) are not named, so base_model null and the true model controller may differ. Tier 2 as a partial pilot (coding tool in use). Only one opened S3+ source; vendor page is S4.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
findings.summary: Syria's communications ministry signed an MoU with aiXplain covering AI infrastructure, data security and training, according to an October 2026 feature.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 MoU; no model or deployment named, so base_model null. Month inferred from the article's 'February' in context of 2026. Same provider as SYR-004; possibly the framework under which the Syriatel deal sits.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or deployments found; Enterprise AM (Oct 2026) reports a GPU shortage and US export-control over-compliance

applications.null_reason: one search found no reputable reporting on safe-city or surveillance systems or vendors in Syria

research_gaps: Whether Syria proceeded with, or dropped, the Chinese purchase for telecom towers and ISP infrastructure after US State Department pressure in Feb 2026 (would be a reversal, reason geopolitical, if dropped).

Equipment vendor(s) Zain chooses for the former MTN Syria network (licence awarded 30 Jun/1 Jul 2026, USD 747m bid, 25 years, 25% state stake; brand launch Q1 2027): Huawei retention or rip-and-replace?
SilkLink (stc): fibre/transmission equipment vendor, who operates the network, data-centre locations, and the 800m vs 675m value discrepancy.
RAN/core split of Huawei's >50% share at Syriatel and MTN, and the other vendor(s) supplying the remainder; Syrian Telecom (fixed) vendors not checked.
Starlink is not licensed (Jul 2026); regulator declared unlicensed terminals illegal Jan 2025 and a licensing study is reportedly under way. Watch for a licence.
Wafa Telecom licence (new national mobile player) seen in search results, not opened: vendor and status.
Surveillance / safe-city systems under the post-2024 government (and legacy Assad-era systems) not established.
MTN exit (announced 2021, formal 2026) was attributed to judicial guardianship and regulatory demands, not sanctions; not coded since MTN is an operator, not an equipment controller.
